links.comparator_used: Model trained only on South American (single-source) public spectra and applied to Kazakhstan samples as-is, versus retraining on pooled South American plus Kazakhstan data
links.outcome: Detection accuracy on Kazakhstan samples by class (SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI, asymptomatic controls)
links.effect: Single-source pipeline as-is: 91.0% SARS-CoV-2+, 48.0% NCARI, 67.0% AC (random forest). Pooled SA-Kaz retraining: 88.0% SARS-CoV-2+, 95.0% NCARI, 78% AC (SVM-RBF), SARS-CoV-2 vs rest ROC AUC 0.983 [0.958, 0.987]; high accuracy maintained for South American samples.
links.tradeoff: SARS-CoV-2+ detection was slightly lower after retraining (88.0% vs 91.0%). The authors note that clinical lab implementation will need continuous optimization as respiratory infections evolve.
links.quote: After re-training of the ML algorithms on the SA-Kaz peak intensity matrix, the accuracy of detection by the top-performing Support Vector Machine with radial basis function kernel model was at 88.0, 95.0 and 78% for the Kazakhstan SARS-CoV-2+, NCARI, and AC subjects, respectively with a SARS-CoV-2 vs. rest ROC AUC of 0.983 [0.958, 0.987]; a high differentiation accuracy was maintained for the South American SARS-CoV-2 and NCARI.

design_hint: local retraining/recalibration of ML model on local data before deployment
